meta_description: Compare Blox Fruits enchantments by category, eligible item, level range, effect, and scroll availability.
intro_md: Enchantments modify weapons and fishing rods with normal levels, unique tradeoffs, rod skills, blessings, or curses. Their value comes from eligible equipment and the way each effect changes a build.
description_md:
## Start with the eligible item

Applies to separates weapon enchantments from fishing-rod enchantments. Check this field first, because a powerful effect is irrelevant when the target item cannot receive it.

## Compare normal and unique effects

Normal enchantments can scale across listed levels. Unique effects occupy their own role and often include a meaningful tradeoff, so read the full Effect instead of comparing only the label.

## Treat blessings and curses as special results

Blessings are rare positive rolls, while curses add strong mechanics with costs or conditions. Rod skills and the rod ability alter fishing actions rather than basic combat stats. Use Category and Level range together to understand what kind of roll you are planning around.
how_it_works_md: Category identifies the enchantment family, Applies to shows eligible equipment, Level range records scaling or slot behavior, and Effect explains the exact gameplay change.

description_json.Unique: Single-slot weapon effects with distinct mechanics or tradeoffs.
description_json.Rod skill: Enchantments that replace the rod's active skill.
description_json.Blessing: Rare beneficial special rolls for weapons or rods.
description_json.Curse: Very rare special rolls with powerful effects and costs.

faq_json.q: Can every enchantment go on every item?
faq_json.a: No. Use Applies to to separate weapon and fishing-rod enchantments.
It shows whether the effect scales through normal levels or occupies a unique or special slot.
They are distinct weapon effects that use a unique slot and may include tradeoffs.

faq_json.q: How are blessings different from curses?
faq_json.a: Blessings are rare beneficial rolls. Curses add powerful mechanics with penalties or conditions.
They are abstract modifiers and the verified source does not provide a distinct icon for every named effect.
